contracts: An opaque native preview retains its admitted original intent. Effects require the exact live-owner witness and current write policy; callers cannot supply an arbitrary replacement AST or mutable candidate.

Preparation executes the existing native commands or compound rich-range action on a disposable staged owner. The result must equal the preview and create exactly one ordinary native Undo group with an empty Redo stack.
Prepared or discarded candidates do not change the source's content, UI, counters, native history, checkpoint, update frame or open natural typing group.

Original/general/document semantic families and ordinary/natural histories retain their existing meanings. No family is silently enabled. Document drafts explicitly select document scope on the candidate, including when already selected.

The effect identity contains the original proposal ID, exact version-two writer receipt and semantic start counter. Immutable preparation belongs to the transport group but precedes the semantic span and must not be selectively undone.

The complete candidate checkpoint, full update frame and one atomic writer group pass existing budgets before preparation returns. Commit consumes that exact candidate under its original guard, without rerunning commands or allocating counters.

The host must serialize prepare, durable decision append and commit, authenticate account/roles and admit/retain referenced assets. Native preparation or an effect descriptor is not an Accept decision, durable acknowledgement or authority credential.

A dedicated host writer does not reserve/fence the user's ordinary stream. The existing native history belongs to the effect writer; importing the effect does not silently transfer it into the accepting user's stack.

Checked public native diff/application can invert the tested semantic spans on a separate writer while retaining peer text and original formatting priority. These private disposable tests expose no generic inverse or accepting-user history API.
